newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close slightly higher, seen flat.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close slightly higher, seen flat.

text.p: Argentine stocks stretched their shy recovery at the close Wednesday on rising volume and were seen caught in a narrow range, dealers said.

"Today we saw the private pension funds returning to the market and keeping it stable," said Jose Napoli of brokers Ignoto y Napoli. "This inflow of funds soaked up fresh selling caused by the bad U.S. inflation number." The U.S. consumer price index came in stronger-than-expected at 0.3 percent.
Blue chips firmed 0.3 percent to close at 708.85 on the weighted MerVal index .MERV. On Tuesday it rose 0.6 percent after sinking to a five-week low Monday.

"Between now and next Tuesday, when the Federal Reserve meets, the MerVal will probably stay rangebound with players quietly building up their positions and speculators kept in check," another trader said.
She noted the bolsa stayed firm Wednesday despite a new climb in U.S. long bond yields perilously close to the psychological barrier of seven percent.
"It seems we've found a floor," the trader said.
Floor volume recovered to 26.1 million pesos from 19 million Tuesday and 15 million Monday, while over-the-counter deals eased to 129.1 million pesos from 134.6 million Tuesday.
The broad market closed unchanged, with winners outpacing losers 31 to 24 and 15 issues closing flat.

Main-tier gains were driven by stocks not traded as ADRs. Top performers were foods giant Molinos, carmaker Ciadea and steelmaker Acindar, which tacked on 2.2 percent, 1.6 percent and 1.2 percent, respectively.
Losers were led by carmaker Sevel, which fell 1.6 percent, gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, off 1.1 percent, and Telecom and oil giant YPF, both off 0.9 percent.
